messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED: spike in 5xx + latency on inference-serving-prod. alert_id=inc-2026-04-12-031. Possible KV cache amplification after batch config rollout.

maya: ack, I'm on it. linking dashboards and rollouts.

ops-bot: metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/kv-cache?orgId=1&from=now-30m to=now — prefix miss rate jumped from 2% -> 38%, continuous batching tokens/sec up 4x. HPA CPU scaling oscillating.

leo: seeing repeated pod creation/termination in logs. stack traces show long tail locks when cache size hits ~2GB.

maya: root cause hypothesis: new batching config reduced batch flush threshold -> more small batches -> higher KV churn and cache thrash -> cache eviction spike -> perf cliff -> HPA flaps.

priya: customer impact: observed elevated 503s for some Dedicated tenants (AcmeCorp) and higher p95 latency on hosted endpoints. CS alerted.

devin: attaching recent autoscaler events: ```
Events:
  Normal  SuccessfulRescale  1m (x12 over 15m)  horizontal-pod-autoscaler  New size: 12; reason: CPU threshold
  Normal  SuccessfulRescale  45s (x8 over 10m)  horizontal-pod-autoscaler  New size: 4; reason: CPU dropped
```

maya: initiated mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout of batching config (rollback to v2026-04-11), 2) bump HPA minReplicas from 3 -> 6, 3) enable short warmup window to avoid immediate downscale for 5m. Doing steps now.

leo: rolling back batch-config to v2026-04-11: `kubectl -n serving set image deployment/batcher batcher=registry.redwood/batcher:v2026-04-11`

ops-bot: deploy bot: rollout started for deployment/batcher. watch: kubectl rollout status deployment/batcher -n serving

maya: patching HPA: `kubectl patch hpa inference-runtime -n serving --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":6}}'` and adding stabilization window: `spec.behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds=300`

priya: opened priority support ticket for impacted customers and added mitigation notes. tagging account teams.

devin: after rollback + hpa patch: prefix miss rate trending down from 38% -> 8% over 12m. pod churn reduced. tail latency p95 improving but still slightly elevated.

maya: still seeing a small oscillation in KV cache occupancy when traffic bursts hit. I want an additional short-term guard: disable continuous batching for hot-prefixes (hotfix config) to reduce KV churn. Suggest applying a quick config flag: `continuous_batching.hot_prefixes=[]` for now.

leo: applying hotfix for hot-prefix exclusion via configmap edit and restarting batcher pods gracefully. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/batcher -n serving`

ops-bot: deploy bot: batcher restart complete. no error.

devin: verifying HPA stability: no new SuccessfulRescale events for 6m. CPU variance within expected.

priya: CS update posted: "Mitigations in progress, reduced impact, monitoring. Will follow up with RCA once stabilized." :white_check_mark:

maya: brief incident summary for handoff: - cause: aggressive batching config lowered flush thresholds causing KV cache churn and evictions -> perf cliff -> autoscaler thrash. - immediate mitigation: rollback batching config, increase HPA minReplicas to 6, set scaleDown stabilization to 300s, exclude hot prefixes from continuous batching. - impact: elevated p95 and intermittent 503s for some Dedicated tenants; mitigations reduced impact within 15m.

maya: leaving handoff to james (next on-call) — please keep watch for recurrence over next 4 hours, escalate to infra if cache eviction rate > 10% or SuccessfulRescale events > 3 within 10m.

james: taking handoff. noted the escalation thresholds. I'll sync with platform tomorrow about safer rollout checks for batching tunables.

maya: tagging runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-batching for RCA template and postmortem. Also created follow-up ticket: INF-7823 (investigate warmup heuristics + rollout gating).

leo: quick TODOs before signoff: add canary traffic test for batching change that watches prefix miss metric, and add HPA behavior test in CI to catch rapid flapping.

james: understood. setting alert suppression for next 30m to avoid noisy pages while tests run.

oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2 -> triage. Incident closed for paging, follow-up ticket INF-7823 assigned.

maya: thanks team. handing off. :handshake:
